title: Dataset state at the start of Round 1
body: LABELS (data/output/pair_labels.csv, 1,447,172 rows, one per ingredient-condition pair). Derived from the OHDSI Common Evidence Model: 4,276 RxNorm ingredients x 5,631 standard OMOP condition concepts, about 6% of all possible pairs. 99.3% of rows come from FAERS/AEOLUS only, 9,908 from SemMedDB only, 486 from both. in_eu_label is FALSE on every row and eu_label_count is null throughout: the EU product-label layer did not survive the CEM build's join to standard condition concepts. This is documented upstream in the local-postgres skill as a known trap, not an export error. Consequence: the efficacy side of the label rests on roughly 7,900 SemMedDB TREATS/PREVENTS assertions and nothing else. y_faers_signal (Evans et al. 2001: PRR>=2 & chi-square>=4 & cases>=3) is positive on ~11% of pairs; y_semmeddb_causes ~0.1%; y_semmeddb_treats ~0.5%. faers_ror is identical to faers_prr in this extract. Median case count is 2 and median PRR 1.36, so most rows are noise at row level. Absence of a pair is NOT a negative: it may mean no effect, never prescribed, or never reported.

title: Condition side: ontology mapping and coverage ceiling
body: data/input/condition/condition_ontology_map.csv maps all 5,631 conditions; 4,444 (78.9%) carry a recommended mapping. Primary source is OMOP2OBO (Callahan et al., Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.7250177), which alone covers 4,138 (73.5%) at concept level; the Bridge fallback tiers add 306 more. OMOP2OBO agrees with an authoritative SNOMED SCTID cross-reference on 97.0% of 1,936 overlapping conditions, which cross-validates both methods. Tiers are recorded per row in match_tier: A1/A2 OMOP2OBO manual curation, A3-A5 OMOP2OBO automatic, B1 authoritative SNOMED xref, B2/B3 lexical, B4 LLM-adjudicated. B4 is about 85% precise on cases where candidate retrieval succeeded, but retrieval only surfaced the correct term 31% of the time, so B4 recall is unknown. A sensitivity analysis restricted to A1/A2/B1 is cheap and worth running. OMOP2OBO ancestor-category rows are EXCLUDED from the gene join: they map a concept to a broad parent (Neoplasm of uncertain behavior of larynx -> 'disorder by anatomical region') and are not equivalences. They are usable as groupings only. TWO ARMS are required because no single resource covers this outcome set. Open Targets' disease index holds only 2,322 HPO terms, and just 424 of the 1,406 HPO terms we map to are in it, so symptom-type conditions are largely absent; conversely HPO carries no SNOMED cross-references (stripped for licensing) so it is reachable only via OMOP2OBO or name matching. The 1,187 unmapped conditions are 958 Disorders and 229 Clinical Findings, led by Upper abdominal pain, Late effect of contusion, Burning sensation, Febrile neutropenia, Injection site pain. These are clinical-encounter concepts with no disease-ontology counterpart anywhere, they are disproportionately high-degree in CEM, and they are not fixable by better matching.

title: Condition feature tables available, and the Open Targets gap
body: READY: condition_features_basic.csv (5,631 rows) with SNOMED concept_code, concept_class_id (4,724 Disorder / 907 Clinical Finding), record_count (occurrences across the OHDSI network, from Hecate - an external frequency measure, not a function of the labels), n_omop_ancestors (mean 8.3 at parentlevels=3), arm, is_mapped, best_match_tier, n_ontology_terms, n_hpo_genes, n_groups. condition_group_long.csv (10,554 rows, 4,279 conditions) gives 23 HPO organ systems plus Open Targets therapeutic areas. condition_gene_hpo_long.csv (2,244,725 rows, 3,322 conditions) is the phenotype-arm gene layer from HPO phenotype_to_genes. CAVEAT on that gene layer: median 133 genes per condition, because HPO annotations are propagated up the hierarchy so a general term inherits every gene beneath it. A high gene count therefore means LOW specificity. Raw counts and unweighted overlaps will mislead; IDF-style weighting is probably needed. NOT READY: the disease-arm gene layer. The Open Targets association_by_datatype_indirect pull is still streaming (41 parquet parts, filtered to the 3,342 of our terms present in their disease index). Until it lands there are no per-datatype genetic evidence scores and no pathway-overlap features, which is why Round 1 contains no pathway lane. SEMANTIC WARNING for when it does land: Open Targets gives a continuous 0-1 score per evidence datatype while HPO gives unweighted curated annotations with no strength. Do not average them into one column. Keep separate feature blocks with a source flag, or binarise both and say so.

title: Splits: 50/30/20 grouped by primary target gene
body: data/splits/ holds train.csv, validate.csv, test.csv plus split_assignment.csv and split_provenance.json, regenerable by scripts/build_dataset.py. Verified from the written files: zero ingredient overlap and zero group overlap between all three fold pairs, all 4,276 ingredients and all 1,447,172 pairs accounted for, shares exactly 0.50/0.30/0.20. Label rates are balanced across folds (y_faers_signal 10.99 / 11.73 / 11.19%). GROUPING UNIT is the primary target gene from ingredient_target_long.csv: 363 groups over 1,541 targeted ingredients, largest 55 (HRH1). Untargeted ingredients are singletons. Full connected components of the drug-target graph were REJECTED as the default because promiscuous targets merge 638 ingredients (41.4% of targeted ones) into one giant component, making a 50/30/20 split unachievable. That scheme is retained as --scheme target_component for a leakage worst-case check. Conditions deliberately appear in multiple folds: the task is generalising to unseen DRUGS, not unseen diseases. 171 conditions in test do not appear in train. Drug and condition degree must be computed from train only; computing them over the full table leaks validation and test information into training features.

title: Drug side: coverage and quarantined columns
body: data/input/drug/ holds ingredient_features.csv (4,280 x 159), target_features.csv (1,536 x 61), ingredient_target_long.csv (8,088 ingredient-target-gene edges covering 1,541 ingredients and 790 genes) and ingredient_features_label_adjacent.csv. ingredient_features_label_adjacent.csv is QUARANTINED: it holds CEM degree terms that are functions of the labels. Use it only as a nuisance control when analysing bias, never as a predictor. Coverage: 2,932 of 4,280 ingredients (68.5%) match a ChEMBL molecule and only 1,716 (40.1%) have a mechanism with an assigned target, so missingness is large and is itself informative. Unmatched ingredients are mixtures, biologics and blood products, minerals and ions, botanicals, excipient-like substances and placebo; they carry only 5.8% of CEM pairs (median CEM degree 6 versus 157 for matched ingredients), so the gap is not worth chasing. Model missingness explicitly rather than imputing it away. Fuzzy name matching to ChEMBL was rejected: a difflib >=0.93 pass produced 68 candidates with many wrong in ways that inject false biology (4-hydroxybenzoic acid -> salicylic acid, factor IX -> factor X). Only exact-normalised and qualifier-stripped matches are used; fuzzy candidates live in review-only columns no feature reads. Check data_dictionary.csv (245 rows) before selecting columns.

title: Round 1 plan: establish the floor and measure the bias structure
body: Eight independent lanes, all runnable in parallel, specified in lab/round_01.md and lab/round_01.json. No pathway-overlap or graph lane this round: the disease-arm gene layer is still pending, and the correct scientific order is to establish what observation bias alone explains before adding biology. Lane 5 (same-target neighbour signal) is the exception and carries real biological signal with no condition genes required. Lane 4 (drug + condition, no interaction) is the project's null hypothesis: if it matches what Round 2's pair-level biology achieves, the bridge hypothesis is not supported.

title: Same-target neighbour transport across the primary-gene group boundary
hypothesis: A train-only shrunk neighbour flag-rate beats the degree floor on validate pairs with >=1 neighbour, and the gain decays as similarity loosens from shared gene to shared protein class.
approach: Three similarity tiers (gene, protein-class leaf, protein-class L1), empirical-Bayes shrinkage k=10 toward the condition's train rate, leave-one-drug-out on train rows, HistGBM, AP by neighbour-count bucket.
label: y_faers_signal
split: train/validate, grouped by primary target gene

title: Two-way-demeaned log PRR residual as the modelling target

findings: +0.062 AP (model B vs degree-only A) on the 33.6% of validate pairs with >=1 gene-level train neighbour (conditional AP: A=0.1272, B=0.1889); unconditional AP is diluted by the 66.4% of pairs with no gene neighbour (A=0.1226, B=0.1687). Decay curve by n_neighbours_gene bucket: 0: A=0.120 B=0.158 (n=288357), 1_2: A=0.138 B=0.189 (n=47983), 3_5: A=0.130 B=0.187 (n=35259), 6plus: A=0.118 B=0.190 (n=62552). Tier decay: model B AP on pairs where only class_leaf similarity is available = 0.2016; only class_L1 available = 0.1222 (vs conditional gene-tier AP 0.1889) -- gain does not monotonically shrink as the tier loosens; inspect whether this reflects a class-level effect rather than target-specific pharmacology per the falsification criterion in the spec. Leave-one-drug-out sanity check: train CV AP (0.2796) vs validate conditional AP (0.1889), gap=0.0907 (no sign of self-leakage). Design note: the gene-tier 'primary gene' refinement uses ChEMBL's own disease_efficacy flag to mean 'primary target', not the split's group_key (group_key-based sharing would always be 0 on validate by construction of the grouped split, which would be a degenerate, not a meaningful, feature). Coverage table reproduced on unfiltered edges per the spec's stated measurement method; the gene-tier subunit-expansion exclusion (component_relationship COMPLEX/FAMILY rows) is applied only to the modeling features, not to the coverage reproduction, since the spec describes the coverage numbers as measured before that fix.
next_steps: If the gene-tier gain holds and decays as class-level tiers loosen, proceed to Round 2 pathway-overlap features restricted to target-specific biology. If gain is flat/increasing with looser tiers, redirect toward class-level priors instead.

findings: Residual model: validate Spearman rho=-0.3064 on n=206585 rows (null rho=0). Two-way fixed-effects structure removed R^2=0.4700 of the variance in log(faers_prr) on train, fit by alternating demeaning (train only, applied unchanged to validate; unseen drugs/conditions get offset 0 and are reported as a separate subgroup in <exp_id>_subgroups.csv). Binary comparison on the identical case_count>=3 subset: classifier validate AP=0.4691 vs degree-only baseline AP=0.4301 (prevalence stated in <exp_id>_run_notes.txt). Four-cell trained-on x evaluated-against table is in <exp_id>_target_comparison.csv: compare the residual model's AP against the binary flag and the binary model's Spearman rho against the residual to judge whether the residual model also ranks the flag competitively (the strong result) or only wins on its own target. Recommendation: see <exp_id>_target_comparison.csv and the rho/AP values above for whether later rounds should switch target -- if validate_spearman_residual is near zero while the binary AP clears its baseline by a wide margin, the recommendation is to NOT switch, since the features are predicting reporting structure rather than a degree-free pharmacological signal; if rho clears 0.10 and the residual model also ranks the binary flag competitively, the recommendation is to switch later rounds to the residual target. This subset (47.6% of rows, case_count>=3) is not a random subsample -- it is biased toward well-reported pairs, correlated with drug age and market size, so these numbers are not directly comparable to exp02's headline AP on all rows.
next_steps: Pull results/<exp_id>/ from the bridge-results volume and inspect <exp_id>_subgroups.csv for the case-count-stratum breakdown before generalizing the headline rho -- if signal is concentrated in the 21+ stratum, the 'closer to causal' claim needs that qualifier per the spec's traps section.

findings: Evans-label (y_faers_signal) validate AP is 0.1208 against a validate prevalence of 0.1173 (spec states 11.7%). See exp_20260922_f2c2c3_feature_ranking.csv for which single count (drug_degree, condition_degree, or condition_record_count) carries the most signal per label, and exp_20260922_f2c2c3_ap_table.csv for the logistic-vs-HistGBM AP gap per label (the gap measures how much non-linearity the three counts can support). The single-feature AP ranking did NOT hold across all five label definitions (see feature_ranking.csv for the per-label values and pairwise Kendall tau); the label-definition sensitivity is now mandatory for downstream reporting.
next_steps: If the ranking held, proceed to exp02 (intrinsic feature blocks) reporting against the Evans label only. If it flipped, carry all five label definitions through exp02-exp05.

findings: YES -- the efficacy half of the project is workable on y_semmeddb_treats using mechanism-only features: validate AP (design M) = 0.1275 against >= 3x prevalence (0.0145, prevalence=0.0048). M vs M+I gap = +0.0686 (AP_M+I=0.1961, AP_I(indication-only)=0.0467) against a 3-seed AP spread (std) of 0.0324 on design M (budget fallback: cut from 5 to 3 seeds because the I-block cardinality fix grew I from 7 to ~97 columns, per the spec's own fallback order); the gap exceeds that spread, so it is claimed as real rather than noise. first_approval importance rank in M+I = 13.0, summed ATC-feature importance = 0.0000 in M+I; drug age and ATC features do not dominate the M+I model (see exp_20260922_7c2e17_importance_top25.csv). Secondary target y_semmeddb_causes was skipped this run (budget fallback, after cutting to 3 seeds and 2-fold CV) because the I-block cardinality fix pushed real per-fit cost above the spec's original budget assumption. M+I train CV AP was also skipped (314-col design, budget exhausted); only the M design CV AP is reported. Recommendation: mechanism-only features already carry transportable efficacy signal; an indication layer would still help but is not gating further modelling. Step 5 (exp03-style gene-tier neighbour feature vs TREATS) was not attempted this run due to budget; see step5 note in run logs and exp_20260922_7c2e17_column_assignment.csv for the audited M/I split.
next_steps: If mechanism-only AP clears 3x prevalence and the M vs M+I gap is small relative to seed spread, proceed to feature expansion on the M side (e.g. exp03's gene-tier neighbour rate against TREATS, not yet attempted here). If not, treat this as the decision-grade negative result gating investment in an indication layer.

title: Label ceiling from independent evidence, and the incumbent FAERS comparator
hypothesis: An evidence stream independent of FAERS ranks y_faers_signal within drug at drug_macro_auc 0.60-0.75, and FAERS disproportionality ranks SemMedDB-asserted harms at a similar level; both bound what any feature set can do.
approach: Within-drug ranking in both directions plus a p_c floor on the independent target, 1,000-resample bootstrap CIs over drugs, emitting a machine-readable success criterion. Adjudicated reference set handed to Claude Code.
label: y_faers_signal
split: validate only (no fitting)

title: Honest nested intrinsic ablation on drug_macro_auc, with a leak audit
hypothesis: With the faers_case_count label term removed and p_c carried as a baseline column, drug-intrinsic features add >=0.02 drug_macro_auc over the 0.576 floor while condition-intrinsic features add less.
approach: Re-run of exp02's four nested designs on a clean degree block; grouped 3-fold CV scored on drug_macro_auc; bootstrap CIs over drugs; mechanism-subset refit; reusable leak_audit.py with blacklist, per-feature AUC screen and a train-validate gap assertion.
label: y_faers_signal
split: train/validate, grouped by primary target gene

title: Within-drug log-PRR residual: a target that exists on held-out drugs
hypothesis: Removing only the condition level and evaluating within drug yields macro within-drug Spearman >= 0.10 on validate, and that ranking scores drug_macro_auc on the Evans flag competitively with the intrinsic union.
approach: One-way condition demeaning on train applied to validate; within-drug rank correlation as the metric so the unlearnable drug level is differenced out of the metric rather than imputed to zero in the target; four-cell cross-target comparison on identical rows; case-count strata.

findings: Ceiling (SemMedDB harm evidence ranking y_faers_signal, validate): drug_macro_auc=0.4990, 95% bootstrap CI over 13 eligible drugs = [0.4858, 0.5155]. n_drugs_scored=13 is < 50, treated as UNDERPOWERED -- the CI, not the point estimate, is the result. Incumbent (log(faers_prr) ranking SemMedDB-harm target, validate): drug_macro_auc=0.5042. Floor on the same (SemMedDB-harm) target (train-only p_c lookup): drug_macro_auc=0.6149 -- this is a fresh number, not the Round-1 0.5759 y_faers_signal floor. Revised solved_threshold = floor(0.5759, y_faers_signal) + 0.5*(ceiling-floor) = 0.5374, reported provisionally pending the adjudicated reference set per the spec hand-off since the ceiling is underpowered. Benefit-direction counterpart (SemMedDB benefit evidence ranking y_semmeddb_treats): drug_macro_auc=1.0000 over 60 eligible drugs, reported separately, not pooled with the harm numbers. Ran on Modal (not locally) despite the spec noting this is cheap enough to run locally, for consistency with exp01-05's execution path and labnotebook logging.
next_steps: Hand off the adjudicated-reference-set spec (OMOP reference set / EU-ADR / OHDSI negative controls) to a Claude Code session per this experiment's own hand-off section -- that requires unrestricted network access this Modal container does not have. Until that lands, success_criterion.json carries source='semmeddb_proxy' and downstream experiments (exp07-10) should read solved_threshold from that file rather than hardcoding 0.65.

title: Gene and pathway overlap between drug targets and condition genes
hypothesis: Genetic-evidence-weighted overlap between a drug's target genes and a condition's implicated genes adds >=0.02 drug_macro_auc over the intrinsic union, concentrated on disease-arm conditions.

title: Why exp_20260922_3f4a30's residual Spearman flips sign between train CV and validate
hypothesis: The sign reversal (train CV rho=+0.489, validate rho=-0.306) is a target-construction artefact, not a weak or anti-correlated model. exp04 builds the target as z - grand_mean - drug_offset - condition_offset, with drug_offset taken from a train-fitted effect and .fillna(0.0) for drugs absent from train (exp04_disproportionality_residual.py:232-239). But the splits hold out whole ingredients by design, so EVERY validate drug is absent from train and every validate row gets drug_offset = 0. The validate target therefore still contains the full drug effect, while the training target had it removed. Model and target are measuring different estimands. Falsifiable predictions: (1) the share of validate rows with drug_unseen is ~100%, not a small tail; (2) the train-fitted drug effect accounts for a large share of validate target variance; (3) evaluating on an estimand where the drug offset is handled consistently - within-drug ranking, or a condition-only demeaning applied identically to both folds - removes the sign flip. If validate rho stays negative under all three, the hypothesis is wrong and the anti-correlation is real.
approach: Diagnostic, no new model class. Reproduce exp04's train-only alternating demeaning on data/splits/train.csv, apply it to validate exactly as exp04 does, and decompose the validate target. Then recompute the evaluation three ways: (a) as exp04 does, (b) Spearman within drug, which is invariant to any per-drug offset, and (c) against a condition-only demeaned target, which is well defined for unseen drugs. Fit is HistGradientBoostingRegressor on train with GroupKFold on group_key, matching exp04; validate touched once at the end. test.csv untouched.
label: faers_prr
split: splits/train.csv + splits/validate.csv, grouped on group_key
notes: Follow-up diagnostic on exp_20260922_3f4a30, not a replacement result. If confirmed, exp04's validate Spearman should not be read as evidence about the residual target.

findings:
Independent reproduction of the exp04 target-mismatch diagnosis, run before exp_20260922_4e79a6 (exp09) was visible and logged after. exp09 reached the same conclusion first and also shipped the fix, so treat this as corroboration, not a new finding. Two things here are additive: an independent reproduction of exp04's exact numbers, and the mechanism for why the pooled correlation lands negative rather than near zero.

Reproduction. Rebuilding exp04's train-only alternating demeaning and applying it as exp04 does gives train CV rho=+0.475 and validate rho=-0.318, against its reported +0.489 and -0.306. So the reported numbers are real and the difference is not a coding slip in exp04's model.

Scale of the mismatch. 100.0% of validate rows are drug-unseen against 0.0% of train rows, so every validate row takes drug_offset = 0. The between-drug component is 0.0% of train target variance and 40.3% of validate target variance: the drug effect is removed from one target and left in the other.

Why negative and not merely weak. Evaluating the same predictions within drug — invariant to any additive per-drug constant — gives rho=+0.400 over 497 validate drugs with >=20 rows, so the flip disappears. The predictions correlate with the omitted per-drug offset at rho=-0.481, and because that offset carries 40% of the validate target's variance, the pooled statistic tracks it instead of the within-drug ranking. That is the specific reason the sign inverts; a pure target mismatch on its own would more usually push toward zero.

What this does NOT show. It does not rescue the two-way residual: +0.400 within-drug is measured on drugs whose per-drug level is unknowable by construction, so no pooled score under that target is well defined for held-out drugs. exp09's one-way condition-only target is the right replacement and already reports macro within-drug rho=0.654. exp04's other metrics (two-way R^2=0.470, the AP comparisons) are not revisited. Features here are the three degree terms only, not exp04's full drug+condition block; the artefact is target-side and reproduces regardless. Not superseding exp04, because exp09 already did. No test-set contact.

Reproducibility caveat: the run script is not committed, to avoid colliding with the exp06-exp10 filenames in #17. The method is fully specified above and in the registered approach — rebuild exp04's demeaning, then score pooled and within-drug.
next_steps: Nothing further on this target; exp09 supersedes it. The transferable lesson for later rounds is to report within-drug and pooled correlation separately whenever a target contains a per-drug level term, because a single pooled number cannot distinguish a model that ranks well inside each drug from one that ranks drugs against each other, and under ingredient-grouped splits only the first is estimable.
